cards.title: World Notes: Remembered in Stone
cards.sub: A real person and place behind this week's game
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: Grace Darling became famous all over Britain. People wrote songs and poems about her, and painters came to paint her picture.
She died young, in 1842, and was buried in the churchyard of St Aidan's Church in Bamburgh, near the sea.
A stone monument there shows Grace lying at rest, holding an oar in her hand, so no one forgets the morning she rowed into the storm.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Today you finish your comparison, and think back over the whole year of reading.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll word-part words, edit in passes, and roll long words.
transcripts.guide2: Read both texts one more time. Then answer the questions.

notes.wordParts: Prefixes and suffixes from this year: re- = again, un- = not, trans- = across, inter- = between, -ful = full of, -less = without.
notes.grammar: Year review: capitals for names and the first word, a comma after an opening part, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, and irregular past forms like went and took.
notes.spelling: Long words: find the vowels, split between them, read each chunk, then push the chunks together. Rescue = res + cue.
notes.wgrd: Both texts say courage means acting even when you are afraid. A strong closing says your claim in a new way and tells why it matters.
vocab: having or showing courage; willing to act even when afraid
continuing to try even when things are hard
a quality that shows good character

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Before you finish, say what is alike and what is different about the two texts, in one sentence each. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. After thinking about all four novels, I decided that courage looks different every time. After starts the opening part, and a comma closes it. I is always a capital. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Make up a poem and say it out loud. Name its form and one figure of speech.
mods.script: Your last poem job this week: make up a poem of your own and say it out loud. Then name it, like a poet. Which form did you choose? Which figure of speech did you use?

mods.todo: Say what one part means. Roll the dice. Say what each word means, then check.
mods.script: Quick question: what does un mean? Not! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Unbroken. Not broken. The boat came home unbroken. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.

mods.todo: Choose one word. Write one sentence about a moment from a book.
mods.script: Watch me use a word about a book from this year. Integrity. Lucy showed integrity: she kept telling the truth about Narnia, even when nobody believed her. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about a book.

mods.todo: Fix it in passes. Then tap all seven words that need fixing.
mods.script: Two passes, like an editor. the keepers daughter was brave and she rowed hard. Pass one, capitals: The. Pass two, apostrophes and commas: keeper's, and a comma before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.

mods.todo: Roll the dice. Count the beats and say where they split. Then check.
mods.script: Dice roll: lifeboat! Life, boat. Two beats. Tap Roll the dice, say the word, count its beats and say where they split. Then tap Check my answer.

mods.todo: Read both texts one more time. Then try the Courage Watch below.
mods.script: No new text today. Read both texts one last time, and pick your strongest detail for your closing. Then try the Courage Watch and the questions.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the texts and the books.
mods.script: Four questions today. One, your closing paragraph. Two, your best piece of evidence and why it works. Three, the character from this year who showed the most courage. Four, talk it over with someone at home.

mods.todo: Write your whole comparison: opening, two paragraphs and a closing.
mods.script: Last step: finish. Clara wrote a closing that says her claim in a new way. Put your whole comparison together, and check your capitals and end marks.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Is someone being brave?

items.t: Mira decides that the small boy matters more than her fear.
items.why: That is just what Text 1 says courage is.

items.t: One of the three boys laughs at Mira.
items.why: Laughing at someone is not brave.

items.t: Text 1 says courage can mean trying again after a big failure.
items.why: Trying again when you might fail takes courage too.
